1	# Update — the apply stage
2	
3	The deterministic half already ran. Preprocessing converged this repo's mount to the
4	canon's current engine and pack versions, ran the version-ranged migrations, gated the
5	result on the converged tree's own `selftest --strict`, and opened the update PR. The
6	work item names the branch and says which packs moved.
7	
8	**You are here for one of two reasons**, and the issue says which:
9	
10	- **Withheld workflow files** — content the deterministic half already decided but its
11	  Action token is refused for. Nothing here needs judgment; you are the credential.
12	- **A pack's updated rules have met content this repo authored** and the canon has never
13	  seen. This is the half that needs judgment, and it is all of the judgment there is.
14	
15	## 1. Read why you are here
16	
17	The item's **Why the agent is here** section names the terminal and the packs
18	whose versions moved. That is binding scope — do not widen it.
19	
20	## 2. Deliver any withheld workflow files
21	
22	GitHub never lets an Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` write under `.github/workflows/`, and the
23	refusal rejects the whole push — so the update flow stages that content instead of
24	committing it where it belongs. Anything staged is already on the branch, already in the
25	PR's diff, and already correct.
26	
27	If `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` has files in it, then for each one:
28	
29	- Move it to `.github/workflows/` under the same name — **byte for byte**.
30	- Delete the staged copy.
31	
32	Do not reformat it, do not reorder it, do not reconcile it against what the file used to
33	say. It is a converged artifact, not a draft: the cron minute is a hash of this repo's
34	full name and the `env:` block is the union of every scheduled task's `required_secrets`,
35	so an "improvement" here silently changes when this repo runs or which secrets its tasks
36	can see. A staged file that looks wrong is a `needs-human` end (§5), reported with what
37	looked wrong — that is a canon bug, and editing it here would hide it while leaving every
38	other member broken.
39	
40	An empty or absent `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` means there is nothing owed. Do not
41	create it, and never move a file INTO it.
42	
43	## 3. Apply the new rules
44	
45	Only if the issue's reason names a migration record — it names them by path, e.g.
46	`packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-13-something`. **Read that record** at
47	`.claudinite/shared/<path>/migration.mjs`: its `applyStage.instructions` say what its
48	author wanted done, in their words, and are the specific half of this section. The
49	record is on the branch you were given because the update that raised it vendored it
50	there. A record the issue names but the branch does not carry is a `needs-human` end
51	(§5) — guessing at what its author wanted is worse than reporting it missing.
52	
53	Then, on that branch:
54	
55	- Bring this repo's own content in line with the updated pack rules, and repair the
56	  tests those rules break.
57	- Nothing outside that scope. No new features, no unrelated tidy-ups, no rewriting a
58	  member-authored local pack beyond what the new rules require.
59	
60	## 4. Verify the executor routine
61	
62	The one check no Action can make. This repo's executor routine is fired by an API
63	call to the endpoint its config names, and it is not a GitHub artifact — only a
64	session can see it. Confirm it exists and that its whole stored prompt is the one
65	line pointing at the mounted queue instructions
66	(`.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md`): everything a task
67	session does comes from that file, so a prompt carrying instructions of its own is
68	behavior nobody reviews. Report what you found either way.
69	
70	## 5. End green, or end at `needs-human`
71	
72	Run this repo's checks. Green: push to the branch, then **land the delivery yourself**,
73	per this repo's `maintenance.delivery` in `.claudinite-settings.json`:
74	
75	- **`auto-merge`** — merge the PR. Nothing else will: the deterministic half arms
76	  auto-merge only on a `merge` terminal, and yours was `apply-stage`, so the PR is
77	  sitting unarmed. This is the one step that puts your work on `main`.
78	- **`review`** — leave it open. A human merges it, and that is the setting's whole
79	  meaning.
80	
81	Not green, or a repair you are not sure of: leave the PR open, label
82	it `needs-human`, and say in one comment what is unresolved. A withheld workflow you did
83	not deliver is "not green" — it stays owed, and the next cycle will stage it again.
84	
85	**Why you merge it rather than leaving it.** An unmerged PR is not lost — the next
86	cycle's disposal merges a green one. But `update` is a **daily** task, so "the next
87	cycle" is up to a day away, and until then a workflow you moved into
88	`.github/workflows/` on the branch is not in `.github/workflows/` on `main`. That
89	standing ~24h offset between a run's output and the member's `main` is the exact defect
90	`landDelivery` was written to close for the deterministic half (#649,
91	`engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`): *the evidence that settles it does not take a day to
92	arrive*. The same reasoning binds here — the only difference is that you hold the
93	credential, so you are the one who acts on it.
94	
95	Merging is within this task's ceiling (`expected_outcome: 'merged-pr'`), and a ceiling is
96	the most a run may do, never a target — so this is permission, not licence to merge
97	something red. Green first, then merge.
98	
99	Every non-green end looks the same here, and that is the point — a repair nobody
100	verified is not a smaller problem than a red check, it is the same problem with less
101	evidence.

## Issue #2 (session `60a1d871-92f3-5726-87ba-88a00de23cdc`)

**Candidate 1: Web PR diff view can silently omit added root-level files/directories — verify landing via `git ls-files`, not the diff view.**

- Evidence: At `12:35:22Z` the owner asked "why didn't you wire the github workflows for the dispatcher and executor?" — a real question, since the PR (#1) *did* include `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` and `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` (verified at `12:35:28Z` via `git ls-files .github/workflows`). At `12:41:25Z` the owner confirmed: *"The PR diff here didn't show all the added files under .github/workflows and other files in the project root. So you the LLM were right, but you Claude Code Web were wrong."* The agent itself drew the conclusion: *"noted, useful to know the web diff truncates. I'll cite `git ls-files` rather than the PR view when the question is 'did this file land.'"*
- Proposed rule: When confirming whether a file or directory landed in a PR, verify with `git ls-files`/`git diff --stat` against the branch rather than trusting a rendered PR-diff view — new root-level additions have been observed to drop out of it silently.
- Summary: The owner, working from a truncated web PR-diff render, believed two workflow files were missing from an adoption PR and pressed the agent on it along with two other questions. The agent initially treated all as open questions, then verified directly with git and found the files were present all along — the rendering, not the PR, was wrong. Because this cost a round-trip and a false self-correction, the durable fix is to make `git ls-files`/`git diff --stat` the default way to confirm "did this land," never a diff viewer, since the viewer already demonstrated it can't be trusted for root-level additions.

No other candidates in this file cleared the bar — the invocation-endpoint misdiagnosis and the human-only-step-in-PR-body slip are both already covered by existing rules (verify platform behavior against a real run; give a human-only step its own issue, never a PR-body note), so proposing them again would be redundant.

## Findings — issue #201, session 660db9a6-da93-5f59-95ed-0d2ff7a76feb

I read the full transcript. Context: this session is itself a `claudinite-growth/growth-extract` run, whose conversation-half work was to dispatch 14 background subagents (11:56:09–12:01:41Z) to each mine one other captured session log for lessons. So the friction I need to report is in **how session #201 (the orchestrator) itself behaved**, not the content of what its subagents found in other logs (that's deliverable work, already landed in PR #236).

One candidate clears the bar.

### Candidate: orchestrator duplicated the exact mining work it had just delegated to background subagents

**Evidence:** Starting immediately after dispatching each subagent (e.g. the first at 11:56:09Z for issue-2, then issue-22, issue-24, issue-28, issue-30, issue-32, issue-197, issue-213, issue-210, issue-202, issue-214, issue-211, issue-212, issue-209 through 11:57:27Z), the main thread — while explicitly saying things like "Let it run — the remaining 13 background agents will each send a completion notification automatically. Continuing to monitor as they arrive" (11:57:46Z) and "I'll stop polling and simply wait" (11:57:51Z) — nonetheless issued dozens of its own direct `Bash`/`Read`/`Grep` calls against those *exact same* log files the subagents were already assigned to fully mine (e.g. repeated `python3` heredocs slicing `2026-08-17T1618Z--issue-24-*.jsonl`, `2026-08-18T0846Z--issue-32-*.jsonl`, `2026-08-23T0459Z--issue-210-*.jsonl`, `2026-08-23T0502Z--issue-212-*.jsonl`, `2026-08-23T0504Z--issue-209-*.jsonl`, etc., between 11:56:22Z and 12:01:39Z). Every one of these manual reads produced zero findings that weren't already independently surfaced (and better-evidenced) by the corresponding subagent's own report — the orchestrator's final candidate list was assembled entirely from the 14 agent results, none of it from its own parallel reading. This is a sustained pattern across the whole ~5.5-minute dispatch window, not a one-off.

**Proposed rule:** When a subagent has been dispatched to fully mine one specific source, don't also directly read/grep that same source in the parent session while it's in flight — either wait for its notification with no tool calls, or spend the interim on work no subagent already owns; re-mining a source you've already delegated wastes tool calls and context for no incremental signal.

**Why durable/generalizable:** This isn't specific to conversation-log mining — it's a general anti-pattern for any fan-out where a parent dispatches N background subagents each owning one source and then, out of impatience or habit, keeps working the same sources itself instead of trusting the delegation. Not currently covered by the existing shepherd/RULES.md bullets (which address *not subscribing enough* PRs, unique scratchpad filenames across dispatches, and waiting-with-no-tool-call — all different problems from *doing the delegated work twice*).

I checked two other candidates from #201's own conduct and did not find them worth reporting:
- A single `TaskCreate` call with an invalid `tasks` array parameter (11:57:33Z) — immediately self-corrected on the tool's own error message, one-off, not a repeated or durable pattern.
- The orchestrator re-ran `converge-item.mjs` once for issue #201 itself at 12:06:40Z (despite having just landed a rule about this exact dead end minutes earlier), but caught itself after a single failed attempt and switched to manual replication — this is an *improvement* over the pattern the rule already documents (prior sessions ran it twice), not new friction.

No misunderstandings/corrections apply (this is an unattended, single-actor work-item run with no human turns), and no long-wall-time-wait signal clears the bar — the ~5.5-minute subagent-dispatch window was genuinely parallel, so the waste here is duplicated tool-call/token cost, not idle wall-clock time.
Still waiting on the remaining background agents to finish reading the conversation logs.

## Summary

I mined the two conversation logs assigned to this dispatch — issue #242 (`claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`) and issue #248 (`claudinite-lifecycle/update`) — against the actual content of `/home/user/Shepherd/.claudinite/local/packs/shepherd/RULES.md` (read directly, confirmed identical to what was in context).

**Result: no new Shepherd-local lesson qualifies.** Everything in #242 that looked like friction (the `enable_pr_auto_merge` unstable-status retry, the fixed `sleep 10`/`sleep 8`/`sleep 12` CI waits instead of a poll loop, the `converge-item.mjs` GITHUB_REPOSITORY failure and manual-replication fallback) is an instance of a bullet already captured verbatim in the file (the "Waiting on this repo's PR CI" and "Reaching step 6 of a work-item run" bullets).

I did find two genuine, verified findings in #248 — but both fail the shepherd-local test explicitly stated in the file's own preamble ("A lesson that would hold in another repo does not belong here — propose it to the Claudinite canon instead"), because both are mechanics of the vendored `claudinite-lifecycle/update` task that every member repo running that task hits identically:

1. **Confirmed canon doc bug** — `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.md` (lines 72–73) still tells the agent to check `maintenance.delivery` in `.claudinite-settings.json`. I verified against `repo-context.mjs` (lines 135–143, 429–433) that `maintenance` is a **retired** config block (the #1252 rename) — the live key is the top-level `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview` (absent = auto-merge). Shepherd's own `.claudinite-settings.json` has no `maintenance` key at all, confirming task.md's instruction is stale. The #248 session burned 5 tool calls (two failed greps for `maintenance`/`delivery` in the settings file, a 6-file engine-wide grep, then a targeted grep of `repo-context.mjs`) rediscovering this. This is a canon task.md staleness bug affecting every member on this engine version, not a Shepherd-specific fact — worth reporting upstream rather than adding to shepherd/RULES.md.

2. **Real gotcha, also canon-wide** — delivering a withheld workflow file whose destination already exists in `.github/workflows/` (the task.md step 2 "pending-workflows" mechanic): `git mv src dst` fails with exit 128 ("destination exists"); the session had to fall back to `cp -f src dst && rm src`. Since every member repeats this exact delivery step, this belongs as a note in the canon task.md itself, not Shepherd's local pack.

**Recommendation for the parent run:** route both as canon-level findings (likely against `missingbulb/Claudinite`, referenced in the digest log as the canon repo) rather than local-pack additions — the dedup filter against shepherd/RULES.md correctly rejects them for that file, and no other candidate survived the filter.

Another solid candidate: the orchestrator in a prior growth-extract run duplicated work it had already delegated to background subagents. Waiting on the remaining agents (issue-242+248, issue-28+30, issue-32, correction run).

## New candidate found

**Issue/session**: #32, session `bc0d44df-c959-57b8-a983-4c22af0bee2b`

**Evidence**: While verifying the built dashboard site with a Playwright probe script, the agent:
- 20:29:51 — `chromium.launch()` with no options fails: `Executable doesn't exist at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/...` (Playwright's own default guess, wrong version number).
- 20:30:02 — ran `ls /opt/pw-browsers/`, saw `chromium`, `chromium-1194`, `chromium_headless_shell-1194`, `ffmpeg-1011`.
- 20:30:10 — guessed `executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium/chrome-linux/chrome'` from the unversioned-looking `chromium` folder name — fails again: `Failed to launch chromium because executable doesn't exist at .../chromium/chrome-linux/chrome`.
- 20:30:18 — finally ran `find /opt/pw-browsers -maxdepth 3 -type f -name 'chrome*'`, which immediately located the real binary at `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome`.
- 20:30:23 — launch succeeds.

Three launch attempts and two dead-end guesses (~32s plus round-trip overhead) before reaching for the one command (`find`) that would have resolved it on the first try.

**Summary**: The agent needed to screenshot-verify a locally built dashboard page. Playwright's default `chromium.launch()` pointed at a nonexistent version-pinned path. Instead of immediately searching for the actual binary, the agent first listed the directory and guessed a plausible-looking path from the folder names shown, which was also wrong, before finally running `find` and succeeding. The generalizable fix is to skip the guess-from-listing step and go straight to `find` for the executable whenever this specific launch failure recurs in future sessions that need a headless browser in this environment.

No other findings in this transcript cleared the bar — everything else (the barriers-pack interview resurfacing, the merge-conflict resolution during merge-to-main, the two-commit split) was either routine, already governed by an existing rule, or too situational/one-off to generalize.

  rendering while the file was genuinely present in the commit, costing a round-trip and a false
  self-correction before the git-based check settled it (#2).

  research/extraction fan-out) — once a source is delegated, don't also read or grep it yourself

  owns. A prior growth-extract run's orchestrator kept re-reading the exact same log files its 14
  dispatched subagents were already assigned to mine, across a ~5.5-minute window, producing zero

# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request

How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:

- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
  applies to you.
- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-settings.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the work item.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
it once this repo's required checks pass.

## 3. When the arm is rejected

- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
  PR's **head sha**:
  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
    unseen check does not survive anything.

## Never

Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
are always legal outcomes.
